newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican businessmen slam high pension commissions.
newsitem.headline: Mexican businessmen slam high pension commissions.

text.p: A powerful business group in northern Mexico on Tuesday slammed Mexico's new private pension management firms, or Afores, saying the steep commissions they were charging workers were unjust.

"We are really worried as an institution to see the commissions that are being authorized...they will practically eat up the returns in the first years from the workers contributions," Jose Mario Garza Benavides, head of Monterrey's National Chamber of Commerce, said.

His complaint, aired at a news conference, became the latest sign of a growing chorus of protest against the high fees charged to offset the start-up costs of the Afores, that have already begun to affiliate workers.
Garza Benavides estimated the commissions would provide some $600 million to the Afores in their first year alone, which he said was roughly equivalent to their start-up costs.

He said he would write a letter to the National Retirement Savings System Commission (Consar), that monitors the Afores, complaining on behalf of the chamber's 15,000 members that the commissions were "unjust".
The Afores say recouping their initial investments will take some seven years, and deny they are charging workers too steeply.
